paragraphs: Automotus sells automated curb management systems to cities and airports. The company says it works with cities, airports and fleets to make communities better places to live.

The cameras attach to existing infrastructure such as streetlight poles. Once installed, the system automates data collection, invoicing and enforcement. Commercial drivers pay for curb time without apps or meters, and agencies can optionally apply discounted rates for electric vehicles. Violations are captured as they occur, with the option of notifying enforcement or issuing a citation automatically. Agencies also receive curb and traffic activity data broken down by every type of vehicle.

The company describes data security and individual privacy as priorities set from the start. It states that the technology blurs all faces, de-identifies data and captures only the license plates relevant to payment and enforcement. Its privacy policies are presented as independently audited and validated.

quote.text: CurbSight cameras bring AI to the curb.
